successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the Neo-Inca State round Vilcabamba, entered by the Spanish on 24 June 1572

ledger.x: 1438: Pachacuti creates the Tawantinsuyu at Cusco.

c. 1438: the Chanka confederation is annexed. 'Conquest and annexation of the Chanka confederation to the new Inca Empire'; the page says the exact date is unknown (Rowe 1438; del Busto 1424-25; Dammert 1430-1440) and that afterwards Cusi Yupanqui led a campaign against the Chankas' former allies and…
The central Andes join under Pachacuti.
ledger.cp: Andean highland chiefdoms (Huanca, Yauyos, Atavillos and others; undated on the page)

ledger.x: 1445-1450: Pachacuti conquers the Colla of the northwest Titicaca shore.

c. 1463: Pachacuti brings the Lupaca of Lake Titicaca into the empire. 'The Lupaca were incorporated into the growing Inca Empire by the emperor Pachacuti'; infobox conquest c. 1463. The Inca crushed a Lupaca and Colla revolt c. 1473 under Topa Inca Yupanqui. Cliopatria holds only the Puno edge of the lake until 1497.…
1460s: the Inca conquer Cajamarca.

c. 1470: Topa Inca Yupanqui conquers the Chachapoya (southern Amazonas and the Abiseo basin, the region of chachapoya-culture's review fix). Overview 'about 1470', a later section 'around 1475'; Garcilaso: second half of the 15th century. Cliopatria's Inca shape reaches the Chachapoyas area only in 1497.
1470: the Inca conquer Chimor, the coast from Tumbes to Lima.
The Inca reach Quito and the equator.
ledger.cp: northern highland chiefdoms (Cajamarca, Cañari, Carangue, Quito; undated on the pages)

ledger.x: 1477: the Aymara kingdoms of the Altiplano are Inca land.

c. 1480: the Chincha Kingdom of the south coast is annexed. 'Part of the Inca Empire around 1480', 'a true territorial annexation' under Topa Inca Yupanqui; the Chincha lords kept much of their autonomy. Cliopatria's Inca shape includes the Chincha valley only from 1497.
The Inca reach the Maule and northwest Argentina.
ledger.cp: Diaguita, Huarpe, Omaguaca, Atacama and other peoples of Collasuyu (the list)

ledger.x: 1529: Atahualpa raises the north against Huáscar.
1529: the Inca Civil War turns the highlands into a battlefield.
April 1532: Atahualpa wins.
1532 (April): the north returns to the single Inca state under Atahualpa; the Cañari who had pledged allegiance to Huáscar were massacred.
16 November 1532: the Spanish capture Atahualpa at Cajamarca.
26 July 1533: Atahualpa is garrotted at Cajamarca.
1533: Cajamarca passes to the Spanish with Atahualpa's death; Manco Inca is later installed as ruler (1533).
15 November 1533: Pizarro's force enters Cusco.
Quito falls to Benalcázar and Alvarado.
January 1535: Pizarro founds Lima.
1537 (spring): Manco Inca withdraws from the siege of Cusco, April 1536 to spring 1537, and flees to Vilcabamba.
1537: Manco Inca flees to Vilcabamba and the rest of the empire is Spanish.
1537: Manco Inca founds the Neo-Inca State at Vilcabamba.
1537: the seat of the Inca moves from Cusco to Vilcabamba.
1567: the Neo-Inca State becomes a Spanish vassal after the Treaty of Acobamba.
1571: the vassal status ends (infobox 'Vassal of the Spanish Empire (1567–1571)'); Toledo declares war on 14 April 1572.
24 June 1572: the Spanish enter Vilcabamba.
1572: the last Inca resistance ends.

wars.name: Chanka-Inca War
wars.outcome: Inca victory under Cusi Yupanqui (Pachacuti); Chanka army annihilated; the Chanka confederation annexed; establishment of the Inca Empire (infobox).

wars.name: Inca conquests of Pachacuti, Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac
wars.outcome: Expansion from the Cusco valley to Quito in the north, the Maule in the south, the Collao and Bolivia; 2,000,000 km2 in 1527 (infobox).

wars.name: Colla-Inca war
wars.outcome: Inca victory: the Colla Kingdom and the Lupaca on the northwest shore of Lake Titicaca conquered under Pachacuti.

wars.name: Inca conquest of the Cajamarcas
wars.outcome: 'Inca victory' against the Cajamarcas and the Chimú Empire (List of wars page).

wars.name: Inca conquest of the northern Andes peoples
wars.outcome: 'Inca Victory'; mass killing of the Caranquis at Yahuarcocha (List of wars page).

wars.name: Conquest of Collasuyu and the Mapuche-Inca War
wars.outcome: Inca victory over the Diaguita, Huarpes, Omaguacas and Atacamas (1470s-1490s); a 'pyrrhic victory' against the Mapuche and Picunche (1471-1530), the Mapuches south of the Maule keeping their independence (List of wars page).

wars.name: Rebellion of the Chimú
wars.outcome: 'Inca Victory'; the Chimú leader executed (List of wars page).

wars.name: Inca conquest of Chimor
wars.outcome: Topa Inca Yupanqui defeats Minchançaman; Chimor is incorporated in 1470 (Chimor infobox); the Chimú emperor is moved to Cusco.

wars.name: Inca-Shuar frontier at the Chinchipe
wars.outcome: The Shuar stopped the Inca push into the Amazon near the Chinchipe River 'in 1527' (Inca Empire page); no border moved.

wars.name: Inca Civil War
wars.outcome: Atahualpa's northern army defeats Huáscar's, captures Huáscar (Quipaipan) and seizes Cusco; Atahualpa holds the empire from 1532.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire
wars.outcome: The Spanish take Cajamarca (Nov 1532), execute Atahualpa (29 Aug 1533), enter Cusco (15 Nov 1533), found Lima (Jan 1535); Manco Inca's revolt and the siege of Cusco (April 1536-1537) fail and he founds the Neo-Inca State at Vilcabamba (1537); Viceroy Toledo…

wars.name: Manco Inca's revolt and siege of Cusco
wars.outcome: Manco Inca besieges Cusco from April 1536 to spring 1537, then withdraws and flees to Vilcabamba (1537).

certainty.note: No treaty line: the suyu frontiers and the Maule, Chinchipe and Ecuadorian limits are approximate; Cusco's own ring is the only sharp ground.
The Spanish-held points (Cajamarca, Cusco, Lima) are dated; the Neo-Inca State's limits are 'unclear' on its page.
